identification.summary: Phlox Tempest is Microsoft's name for the actor formerly tracked as DEV-0796, which Microsoft linked to a wide-ranging click fraud campaign in which clicks generated by a node-webkit app or malicious browser extension secretly installed on victim devices are monetized [S2][S3]. Reporting ties the activity to the ChromeLoader browser hijacker [S2][S3].
identification.firstObserved: 2022-09 (earliest public Microsoft attribution to DEV-0796; ChromeLoader itself was reported by Red Canary from early 2022)
identification.notes: Secondary coverage cites a Microsoft Threat Intelligence post from mid-September 2022 as the origin of the DEV-0796 designation [S2][S3]; the original Microsoft post was not opened. ChromeLoader is a malware family, not necessarily a single actor: VMware reported ChromeLoader variants dropping ransomware and other payloads, which this encyclopedia does not attribute to Phlox Tempest [S4][S5]. Do not confuse with Fox Tempest (Microsoft malware-signing-as-a-service actor, 2026), a different actor [S6].

attribution.basis: Cited sources describe the activity as a click fraud (monetization) campaign and do not state a state sponsor [S2][S3]. The encyclopedia record lists origin Israel, but no cited source supports that.

objectives: Financial gain through click fraud: monetizing clicks generated by a node-webkit app or malicious browser extension installed on victim devices [S2][S3].

targeting.notes: Victims are individual users lured by malicious ads or YouTube comments into downloading an ISO file; macOS users were also targeted with DMG files [S2]. Red Canary described ISO lures disguised as cracked games and pirated movies and TV shows, spread via pay-per-install sites and social media [S7]. No sector or country targeting is stated in the sources reviewed.

capabilities.summary: Microsoft-attributed activity used an ISO file, delivered via malicious ads or YouTube comments, that installs a browser node-webkit (NW.js) component or a browser extension [S2][S3]. Related ChromeLoader reporting describes a browser hijacker that changes browser settings [S7], uses PowerShell to inject an extension into the browser, and creates a scheduled task via svchost.exe for persistence [S9]. Which of these variant-level details belong specifically to DEV-0796 versus other ChromeLoader operators is not established in the sources.

campaigns.name: Microsoft click fraud warning (DEV-0796 / ChromeLoader)
campaigns.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported an ongoing, wide-ranging click fraud campaign attributed to DEV-0796, starting with an ISO file from malicious ads or YouTube comments that installs an NW.js app or browser extension; DMG files were seen against macOS [S2][S3]. Coverage places the Microsoft post (tweet) on September 16, 2022 [S3].

campaigns.name: VMware Carbon Black ChromeLoader advisory (adjacent, not attributed to DEV-0796)
campaigns.summary: VMware reported ChromeLoader variants that dropped ransomware (Enigma), stole data and used zip bombs; the Bloom.exe variant first appeared in March and had infected at least 50 Carbon Black customers [S4][S5]. Sources do not show whether this was the same operator as DEV-0796 [S4].

diamond.adversary: Financially motivated click-fraud operator tracked by Microsoft as Phlox Tempest (DEV-0796) [S2][S3].
diamond.capability: ISO and DMG lures installing NW.js apps or malicious browser extensions (ChromeLoader-linked) to generate fraudulent clicks [S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Malicious ads and YouTube comments used as delivery vectors [S2]; no domains or IPs in sources reviewed.
diamond.victim: Individual end users of Windows and macOS browsers [S2]; no sector data.
diamond.technology: Windows and macOS endpoints; Chromium-based browsers and Safari; ISO/DMG file mounting; PowerShell and scheduled tasks [S2][S9].

gaps: Original Microsoft Threat Intelligence post on DEV-0796 not opened; WebFetch could not reach any host in this session, so details rely on search-result summaries of secondary coverage.
No source supports the Israel origin in the encyclopedia record.
No Microsoft report on the Phlox Tempest rename or later activity found.
Relationship between DEV-0796 and the broader ChromeLoader operators (including VMware-reported ransomware-dropping variants) is unresolved.
No victim sector or regional targeting, infrastructure indicators, or operator identity identified.
Malpedia entry could not be verified in search; it is not used as a source.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Thin evidence: a financially motivated click-fraud actor delivering ISO/DMG lures via malicious ads and YouTube comments to consumer browsers [S2][S3]. Relevance to DoD is mainly indirect: personal devices and unmanaged browsers of personnel could carry hijacker extensions. MLCOA (assessed): continued opportunistic adware and click-fraud distribution to general users. MDCOA (assessed): ChromeLoader-style footholds reused to drop heavier payloads such as ransomware, as VMware observed for related variants [S4]. Candidate indicators: ISO/DMG mounted from user downloads, unexpected browser extensions or NW.js apps, scheduled tasks launching via svchost.exe, PowerShell loading extensions [S9].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: track Microsoft and EDR vendor reporting on ChromeLoader and DEV-0796. Authorities: browser-extension and removable-image policy sits with local network owners and DODIN operators. Mission assurance: limit extension installation and ISO/DMG mounting on managed endpoints. Coordination: share any hits with the supporting cyber defense service provider; no tasking beyond routine hygiene is indicated by these sources.
